data.exact_reserve_text: The movement in the net provisions for claims includes a deterioration of GBP 1.7m in respect of reserves set in prior years (2019: deterioration of GBP 0.3m).

prior_year_events.impact_description: Foreign Exchange movement on prior year claims outstanding

named_events.loss_description: The current ultimate estimated losses for Hurricane Laura are gross and net $13.4m, this loss is protected by both surplus reinsurance and excess of loss covers. Hurricane Laura remains covered within the excess of loss programme which offers some protection for deterioration to the net ultimate loss.

The current ultimate gross and net loss is $0.8m. Due to the nature of the COVID-19 loss there may be areas where active contract exclusions exist, it is possible these may be disputed by clients or where cover is granted following legal rulings. The syndicate has and will seek to defend exclusions where appropriate.

data.standardized_narrative: For the 2020 financial year, Syndicate 6103 reported a gross prior year reserve release of GBP 1.675 million. This release was primarily driven by the commutation of the 2017 Year of Account reinsurance to close and favourable foreign exchange movements on prior year balances. The syndicate's business is classified as reinsurance accepted, predominantly covering US property catastrophe risks. During the year, the syndicate was exposed to 2020 events including Hurricane Laura and COVID-19 pandemic losses, with ultimate gross and net losses for these events estimated at $13.4 million and $0.8 million respectively.
data.data_quality_notes: The gross prior year development amount is derived from specific gross movements (RITC and Foreign Exchange) in the Claims Outstanding reconciliation table on page 25, which show a release. This contradicts the narrative text on page 25 which states a 'deterioration of GBP 1.7m' for net provisions in prior years. The gross figures from the table are prioritized. Named events (Hurricane Laura, COVID-19) are quantified in USD, not GBP.
